label: Relatlimab — 2-compartment IV · linear + Michaelis-Menten elimination · time-varying CL · Opdualag BLA 761234
_note: The other half of the Opdualag fixed-dose combination; the nivolumab half is its own spec.

_source.document: Regulatory/11_FDA_M.pdf — CENTER FOR DRUG EVALUATION AND RESEARCH, APPLICATION NUMBER 761234Orig1s000, MULTI-DISCIPLINE REVIEW, Opdualag (nivolumab and relatlimab-rmbw) (Reference ID 4955210)
_source.table: Table 77: Applicant - Parameter Estimates of the Final Relatlimab Population Pharmacokinetic Model (p266-267)
_source.subjects: N = 1713 adults (456 first-line melanoma, 791 prior-IO melanoma, 466 other tumours), Table 74
_source.referenceSubject: Table 77 Note 1 — 'a reference subject, 60-year old white male, weighing 75 kg, with 1L MEL, baseline eGFR of 90 mL/min/1.73 m2, baseline ALB of 4 g/dL, baseline LDH (normalized to upper limit of normal) of 0.8, a normal PS status (PS = 0), and receiving nivo+rela FDC ... These reference values were aligned with the nivolumab PPK model reference values.'

_unitConversions.Vm: VMAX 0.0776 mg/h x 24 = 1.8624 mg/day. Unlike dupilumab, the review gives Vmax as an amount rate, so it is used as is.
_unitConversions.ALB: centred at 4 g/dL in the source; a power model is scale-free, so 40 g/L is identical.
_unitConversions.LDH: the covariate is LDH divided by the upper limit of normal, centred at 0.8. Table 74 reports LDH in U/L (first-line melanoma median 238, mean 355, range 60-4641). Treating the median as the 0.8 reference (the note says the references are the approximate dataset medians) puts the upper limit of normal near 298 U/L; the population distribution below is scaled by that factor.

limitations: Exposure of the reference subject is lower than the population geometric means in Table 26 (steady-state Cmax −15%, average concentration −13%). The reference-subject clearance (6.97 mL/h) is also 15% higher than the population geometric mean reported in the review (6.06 mL/h after the first dose). This appears to reflect differences in covariate make-up between the reference subject and the actual melanoma population; the values still fall within the pass intervals (based on the reported CV).

Between-subject variability on Emax (omega^2 0.101) and the performance-status term on Emax (EMAXPS −0.148) cannot be applied: the former is not supported by the engine, and for the latter the rule for combining it with the main Emax is not printed. This appears to be one reason why the model's late-treatment decrease in clearance (4.9%) is smaller than the label's 'about 10%'.

The LDH covariate is a ratio to the upper limit of normal (ULN), but the distribution table is given only in U/L. The median of 238 U/L was mapped to the reference value 0.8 for conversion (which amounts to assuming a ULN of about 298 U/L). The LDH distribution has a very long right tail (max 4641 U/L), so turning on covariate sampling widens the shaded band considerably.

The review does not print the model equations. Continuous covariates were applied as a power of the ratio to the reference value and categorical ones as exp(theta) — the same inference as for nivolumab.
The model has no separate term for drug–drug interaction with nivolumab. The fixed-dose combination (FDC) is the reference, and separate administration (SAV) is reflected only as a covariate.

Regulatory/11_FDA_M.pdf p92 Table 27 — predicted dose-normalized relatlimab exposures and accumulation ratio by dose, geometric mean (CV%): 160 mg Q4W (N=734) RAC 1.87 (26.5), defined as Cavg,ss / Cavg1 - the same definition the app uses. The label rounds it to 'the systemic accumulation was 1.9-fold'.
Regulatory/10_FDA_L.pdf 12.3 — 'The geometric mean (CV%) volume of distribution at steady state of relatlimab is 6.6 L (20%)'. Computed here as Vc + Vp.

Regulatory/10_FDA_L.pdf 12.3 — 'the geometric mean (CV%) effective half-life (t1/2) of relatlimab is 26.2 days (37%)' after 480/160 mg Q4W. An effective half-life is the one that reproduces the accumulation ratio, so it is computed here as ln2 x tau / ln(R/(R-1)) from the simulated steady state, not from the terminal slope (which, with Michaelis-Menten elimination, depends on concentration).

covariateChecksNote: Table 27 shows dose-normalised exposure and accumulation ratios as the dose is varied from 20 to 800 mg. At lower doses target-mediated (Michaelis-Menten) elimination makes up a larger share, lowering exposure per unit dose, so these rows validate the nonlinear elimination term. Values were converted to concentrations by multiplying by the dose, and intervals were set from the reported CV. The 20 mg sample (21 patients) is small. The clearance rows are the geometric means after the first dose and at steady state from p94 of the review; the ratio has no interval, so ±20% is used.

baselineSource: Regulatory/11_FDA_M.pdf Table 77 — CL0REF 6.97 mL/h (RSE 3.61%), VCREF 4.13 L (1.04%), QREF 25.5 mL/h (4.37%), VPREF 2.97 L (2.25%), VMAX 0.0776 mg/h (4.18%), KM 1.47 mg/L (10.7%), converted to per-day units.
iivSource: Regulatory/11_FDA_M.pdf Table 77 Random Effects — ZCL 0.144 (SD 0.379), ZV1 0.0633 (0.252), ZV2 0.170 (0.412), ZVmax 0.203 (0.451). The %CV here is sqrt(exp(omega^2)-1), at which this engine's omega equals the reported one. ZEMAX 0.101 cannot be applied (see limitations).

effects.source: Regulatory/11_FDA_M.pdf Table 77 — CLALB -0.868 (11.9%); reference 4 g/dL = 40 g/L.
effects.desc: Almost exactly the albumin exponent of nivolumab (-0.965) and pembrolizumab (-0.854).

effects.source: Regulatory/11_FDA_M.pdf Table 77 — CLBLDH 0.991 (14.5%); baseline LDH normalized to the upper limit of normal, reference 0.8.
effects.desc: The app's first tumour-burden marker. Clearance rises almost in proportion to LDH: a patient at twice the upper limit of normal clears relatlimab about 2.5 times faster than the reference. The nivolumab model in the same review keeps no LDH term.

effects.source: Regulatory/11_FDA_M.pdf Table 77 — CLBGFR 0.234 (21.3%), reference 90 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Regulatory/11_FDA_M.pdf Table 77 — CLSEX -0.199 (14.3%), applied as exp(theta) for women (reference: male, Note 1).
Regulatory/11_FDA_M.pdf Table 77 — CLPS 0.120 (21.5%), baseline ECOG performance status 1 or worse.
Regulatory/11_FDA_M.pdf Table 77 — CLSAV 0.156 (19.7%): nivolumab and relatlimab co-administered from separate vials rather than the fixed-dose combination (reference).
effects.desc: Given from separate vials, relatlimab clears about 17% faster than in the fixed-dose combination - a larger effect than the matching nivolumab term (+3%).

effects.source: UNSOURCED — Note 1 gives QREF 'in a reference subject weighing 75 kg', but Table 77 lists no weight exponent for Q, so Q is left unscaled.
UNSOURCED — the reference subject is 60 years old, but no age term appears in Table 77 (the nivolumab model keeps one; this one does not).
UNSOURCED — 7.5% of first-line melanoma subjects were ADA positive (Table 74), but no ADA term was retained in Table 77.
Sourced but not applied — Table 77 EMAXPS -0.148 (24.2%) modifies the time-varying Emax for PS 1 or worse, but the rule combining it with EMAX is not printed.
effects.desc: Left off rather than guessed; it would enlarge the late-treatment clearance drop in patients who are less well.

desc: Relatlimab clearance also decreases during treatment, but far less than nivolumab (maximum 19.8%) — 4.9% —
and the time to half of the change is later, at 133 days. With a Hill coefficient of 4.03, the change is concentrated around that time.
